patient.chief_complaint: Witnessed cardiac arrest resuscitated, now unresponsive — EEG shows burst-suppression, unsure if NCSE or post-anoxic sedation
patient.history_present_illness: A 62-year-old retired firefighter was brought to the emergency department after witnessed cardiac arrest at a gym. Bystanders initiated CPR immediately. EMS arrived 7 minutes after collapse. The patient was found in ventricular fibrillation; two defibrillation shocks achieved ROSC after approximately 11 minutes of cardiac arrest. He arrived intubated with propofol 10 mcg/kg/min infusion for sedation. He is now in the ICU for targeted temperature management (TTM at 36°C). EEG was ordered by the on-call neurology resident due to concern about 'subtle limb movements' observed by nursing — periodic flexion of the left arm and subtle left facial twitching. The night team is unsure whether these movements are (A) myoclonic status epilepticus post-anoxia (malignant, poor prognosis), (B) NCSE from another cause, or (C) post-anoxic myoclonus without EEG correlate (sometimes benign, as in action myoclonus-renal failure syndrome, or sometimes malignant Lance-Adams syndrome). The patient's wife reports he had a recent syncopal episode 2 weeks ago that was worked up and 'told it was benign.' He takes metoprolol and aspirin for coronary artery disease. His cardiologist called and reports he is on amiodarone loading post-arrest. No prior epilepsy.

No prior epilepsy or neurological disease

neurological_exam.mental_status: GCS 3 (E1V1M1) — intubated, sedated on propofol. No response to voice or light noxious stimuli. No spontaneous eye opening.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 3 mm bilaterally, sluggishly reactive to direct light. Corneal reflex present bilaterally. No doll's eye movements elicited (consistent with sedation).
neurological_exam.motor: Periodic flexion of left arm every 15-20 seconds observed by nursing. Subtle left facial twitching synchronous with arm jerks. No spontaneous purposeful limb movements. All limbs flaccid at rest between myoclonic jerks.
neurological_exam.additional: Patient intubated and on TTM at 36°C. Left arm periodic flexion at approximately 15-20 second intervals. Subtle left perioral twitching. These movements are the reason for urgent EEG consultation.

eeg.impression: This is an ABNORMAL EEG. 1. Burst-suppression pattern — generalized, with left hemisphere predominance during bursts; inter-burst intervals 4–8 seconds. 2. Left hemisphere sharp waves embedded within bursts, maximal at T3. 3. Mild EEG reactivity to external stimulation present on this recording. Electroclinical correlation: left-sided periodic limb movements time-lock to left hemisphere burst activity. Concurrent sedating medications noted (see clinical history). Clinical correlation recommended.
eeg.limitations: Propofol infusion is noted in the clinical record; its contribution to the burst-suppression pattern cannot be excluded from EEG alone. Repeat recording after sedation adjustment may be informative.
recommended_actions: Repeat EEG after adjustment of sedating medications

output.impression: This is an ABNORMAL EEG (repeat recording). 1. Burst-suppression pattern persists — generalized, with left hemisphere predominance; inter-burst intervals now >10 seconds. 2. Left hemisphere sharp waves (T3–F3) embedded in bursts, electroclinically correlating with left-sided periodic limb movements. 3. EEG reactivity to stimulation is absent on this recording (not present on prior study). Comparison with prior study: burst-suppression pattern unchanged in morphology; inter-burst interval has lengthened and EEG reactivity is no longer elicited. Clinical correlation recommended.

proposed: amiodarone 150 mg IV bolus + 1 mg/min infusion (loading, current)
interactions: Amiodarone + lacosamide: MAJOR — additive sodium channel blockade causing PR prolongation, AV block, and bradycardia; amiodarone loading dose (150 mg bolus + 1 mg/min infusion) already prolongs PR to 240 ms; adding lacosamide can cause complete heart block in this compromised post-arrest heart
Amiodarone + levetiracetam: no pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic interaction; levetiracetam has no sodium/calcium channel effects — safe with amiodarone
contraindications: Lacosamide with concurrent amiodarone loading — risk of complete AV block in hemodynamically compromised post-cardiac arrest patient
warnings: Monitor ECG PR interval when combining agents with conduction effects
Agents with sodium channel blockade have additive PR prolongation risk with amiodarone
output.formulary_status: Levetiracetam IV: formulary. Lacosamide IV: formulary.
alternatives: Valproate IV as second-line if levetiracetam fails — no cardiac conduction effects; check liver function
Phenobarbital IV as third-line — no PR prolongation; respiratory depression risk

output.methodology: Bilateral median nerve stimulation at 56h post-arrest after propofol reduced
output.impression: Bilateral absent cortical N20 responses to median nerve stimulation at 56 hours post-cardiac arrest, obtained after reduction of sedating infusion. Peripheral responses (N9, N13 cervical) are present bilaterally, confirming adequate peripheral nerve conduction and technical adequacy of the study. Bilateral absence of cortical N20 responses is an established electrophysiological finding in the post-cardiac arrest setting. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Extensive diffuse restricted diffusion involving near-total bilateral cerebral cortex with bilateral deep gray nuclei (putamina and thalami). FLAIR hyperintensity corresponds to DWI restriction with loss of cortical gray-white differentiation. The distribution and severity of DWI restriction is consistent with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. No hemorrhage, mass lesion, or arterial territory infarct identified. Clinical correlation recommended.

results.title: Post-anoxic status epilepticus: treatment and prognosis
results.key_finding: In post-cardiac arrest patients, burst-suppression with electroclinical myoclonic correlates is associated with poor neurological outcomes. Antiseizure medication trials (levetiracetam, valproate) are reported in this population; evidence for neurological outcome improvement is limited. EEG reactivity and pattern evolution have been studied as prognostic markers in multimodal post-arrest assessment frameworks.

output.summary: Published evidence on post-anoxic myoclonic status epilepticus documents the prognostic significance of EEG pattern, somatosensory evoked potential findings, and serum neuronal biomarkers in post-cardiac arrest patients. Antiseizure treatment trials are described in the literature; outcome benefit is not established. Multimodal assessment frameworks (EEG, SSEP, neuroimaging, serum biomarkers) are the subject of ongoing investigation and guideline development.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

csf.interpretation: Unremarkable CSF. Normal cell count, protein, and glucose.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Post-anoxic myoclonic status epilepticus (MSE) with burst-suppression EEG after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, presenting diagnostic challenge from concurrent propofol sedation and hypothermia masking EEG interpretation

differential.key_features: Propofol causes dose-dependent burst-suppression; KEY TEST: reduce propofol and repeat EEG — if burst-suppression resolves, it was drug-induced; if persists (as in this case), post-anoxic MSE confirmed
TTM at 36°C (not 33°C) — mild hypothermia rarely causes burst-suppression alone; propofol is more likely contributor; burst-suppression at 36°C suggests post-anoxic injury

differential.diagnosis: Focal NCSE (from treatable cause — autoimmune, metabolic)
differential.key_features: Post-anoxic pattern with diffuse cortical involvement; autoimmune panel negative; no focal lesion; MRI shows diffuse HIE pattern

optimal_actions.action: Urgent EEG to characterize burst-suppression pattern
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Burst-suppression with left hemisphere spike activity correlating with left arm jerking

optimal_actions.action: REDUCE propofol (10 to 5 mcg/kg/min) and repeat EEG in 30-60 minutes — critical step to distinguish drug-induced vs post-anoxic burst-suppression
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Burst-suppression persists after reduction = post-anoxic MSE confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions: amiodarone + AED choice — lacosamide contraindicated, use levetiracetam
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Amiodarone + lacosamide = AV block risk; levetiracetam is safe

optimal_actions.action: IV levetiracetam 1500 mg loading (symptomatic treatment for post-anoxic MSE) — NOT expected to improve prognosis
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Possible mild reduction in myoclonic burden — prognosis unchanged

optimal_actions.action: Serial NSE at 48h and 72h post-arrest for prognostication
optimal_actions.expected_finding: NSE >33 mcg/L at 48h (68) and rising at 72h (82) — very poor prognosis

optimal_actions.action: SSEP after propofol reduction at 48-72h post-arrest
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral absent N20 — 100% specific for poor outcome

optimal_actions.action: MRI brain DWI after TTM completion (48-72h) for extent of injury
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Extensive bilateral cortical DWI restriction — maximal HIE pattern

optimal_actions.action: Goals-of-care family meeting with neurology, cardiology, palliative care after multimodal prognostication complete
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Informed family decision based on poor prognosis markers

critical_actions: Reduce propofol and repeat EEG — cannot interpret burst-suppression without excluding drug-induced artifact
Levetiracetam preferred AED — amiodarone loading precludes lacosamide (PR prolongation/AV block)
Serial NSE at 48h and 72h — prognostication requires delayed measurement, not <24h
Bilateral SSEPs after sedation reduction — most reliable predictor of outcome
Multimodal prognostication before any withdrawal of care decision
contraindicated_actions: Lacosamide in patient on amiodarone loading — additive sodium channel blockade causing AV block
Aggressive burst-suppression induction (propofol/midazolam dose escalation) for post-anoxic MSE — does NOT improve outcomes; prolongs ICU stay without benefit
Prognosticating <24h — early NSE, early EEG findings unreliable; sedation confounds all early results
Withdrawing care without completing multimodal prognostication
key_reasoning_points: Burst-suppression interpretation requires distinguishing drug-induced (propofol/hypothermia) from post-anoxic — the CRITICAL step is sedation reduction trial with repeat EEG
Amiodarone loading + lacosamide = major interaction: both affect sodium channels causing additive PR/QRS prolongation and AV block risk in compromised post-arrest heart
Post-anoxic MSE: AED treatment (levetiracetam) may be given but does NOT improve neurological outcomes — prognosis discussion is the priority
Neuroprognostication requires minimum 72h post-arrest after TTM completion: NSE at 48-72h, SSEPs after sedation reduction, MRI DWI, EEG pattern
Rising NSE trend (18 → 68 → 82 over 72h) = ongoing neuronal destruction = actively deteriorating HIE

red_herrings.data_point: Propofol 10 mcg/kg/min infusion noted in medications
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggest burst-suppression is entirely propofol-induced, leading to under-treatment of post-anoxic MSE
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Propofol can cause burst-suppression; however, sedation reduction trial shows burst-suppression persists — post-anoxic MSE is the primary cause. Propofol contributes but is not the sole explanation.

red_herrings.data_point: Mild EEG reactivity to stimulation on initial EEG
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggest preserved cortical function and reasonable prognosis, potentially delaying goals-of-care discussion
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Initial EEG reactivity is a favorable sign but must be interpreted with full multimodal assessment. EEG reactivity was lost at 4 hours — progressive deterioration. Bilateral absent SSEPs + rising NSE + extensive DWI restriction override initial reactivity sign.
